tasks.name: GT expander subtype registration
tasks.change: Introduce a subtype compatible with GT_Turbine using the existing physics, explicit class ancestry and the existing output contract. Include incompatible and ambiguous bindings.
tasks.oracle: Compatible case reproduces unchanged physical and mechanical outputs; incompatible/ambiguous binding rejects before result publication. Identity and provenance identify subtype correctly.
tasks.gap: Isolated fixture and subtype adapter registration in both arms. Existing class traversal alone must not be described as automatic model discovery.
tasks.novelty_limit: Basic subtype tests already existed. New evidence must concern change propagation across consumers and fair change-cost comparison, not another accepted subtype.

tasks.name: HP steam turbine mechanical model replacement
tasks.change: Replace the HP_ST mechanical implementation with an interface-compatible versioned wrapper around the same numerical kernel. Also test a missing required output.
tasks.oracle: Same operating point gives equivalent outputs; version identity changes; omitted required output rejects without publishing mixed-version results.
tasks.gap: Common versioned wrapper, output-contract fixture, per-arm registration; no new life-prediction model.
tasks.novelty_limit: Only establishes integration costs and contracts, not improved predictive accuracy.

tasks.name: GT-to-HRSG stream interface migration
tasks.change: Expose the same GT exhaust state through a versioned boundary with flow in kg/s instead of kg/hr and temperature in K instead of degC. Normalize at a declared common adapter. Negative cases omit/misdeclare units or supply conflicting values.
tasks.oracle: Converted stream and all downstream process outputs match the original-unit reference within fixed tolerances. Invalid interface rejects at the harness boundary rather than silently producing a plausible value.
tasks.gap: NEW shared boundary adapter and intermodule unit contract needed. Current physical solver is not ontology-rewired. RDF and JSON receive identical converter kernels.
tasks.novelty_limit: Not automatic arbitrary-unit inference or graph-driven flowsheet synthesis.

tasks.name: Steam-water circuit interface migration
tasks.change: Version the complete steam-water boundary manifest and migrate a named steam output or serialized enthalpy units (kJ/kg versus J/kg), preserving numerical kernels and topology. Include wrong source, swapped hot/cold reheat, omitted field and stale version cases.
tasks.oracle: Valid migration preserves complete cycle outputs and mass-energy audit within frozen tolerances. Invalid source, field, unit or version is identified before result acceptance. Return-stream identities remain correct.
tasks.gap: NEW complete intermodule boundary manifest, common adapters and boundary hooks for BOTH arms. Current engineering contract covers GT ports only. Treat the recycle circuit as one coupled subsystem; rerun the full loop.
tasks.novelty_limit: Interface and contract evolution on unchanged topology, not arbitrary flowsheet synthesis, selective downstream scheduling or plant validation.

tasks.name: Operating-scenario revision with whole-process provenance
tasks.change: Change an accepted ambient-temperature or condenser-pressure input from scenario A to B; recompute full process, OperatingPoint, mechanical models, findings and diagnosis. Reuse result containers deliberately; include a delayed A result and failed B run.
tasks.oracle: Accepted B equals a clean fresh B evaluation using the same kernels. No consumer may report A results as current B. Failure retains prior results only if clearly historical/unavailable for B. No expected direction of physical change is assumed.
tasks.gap: Common scenario/revision envelope and explicit consumer dependency manifest needed. Existing graph clearing and frontend session guards are not a generic selective dependency scheduler.
tasks.novelty_limit: Use full reruns first. Stale-result correctness already tested in submitted work; new question is lifecycle/change cost across all consumers. No plant accuracy claim.

tasks.name: HRSG mechanical-output contract migration
tasks.change: Version/rename one HPSH result field while preserving value/unit and existing warning semantics. Update producer, output validation, publication and retrieval; include one deliberately unmigrated consumer.
tasks.oracle: Migrated consumers agree on value, unit, equipment identity and result version. Old results cannot silently satisfy a new field contract. An unmigrated consumer reports incompatibility rather than plausible stale output.
tasks.gap: Versioned common output schema and independent consumer checks; current RDF property map and warning code require explicit edits. Do not invent HPSH Bayesian links; current mechanical Bayesian evidence is compressor-specific.
tasks.novelty_limit: Schema evolution evidence, not KCER acquisition/missing-input results or improved fault-detection accuracy.

arms.A: Current RDF/RDFS implementation plus explicitly listed shared interface additions
arms.B: Centralized typed JSON registry with equivalent hierarchy traversal, validators, conversion kernels, generic relation traversal and lifecycle guarantees
arms.C: Optional semantic ablation: same RDF with closure omitted or pre-materialized; diagnostic arm only, not a deliberately weak primary baseline

metrics: adapter and consumer modification sites (including setup cost separately)
detected and undetected seeded migration inconsistencies (not human error rates)
cold parse/init and warm validation/query time
execution_policy: Separate behavior-preserving migration from physical-input-change tasks.
Freeze expected outcomes and tolerances before arm results are examined.
Derive numerical tolerances from shared-kernel repeatability and published serialization precision, not after seeing which arm wins.
Measure first-time setup separately from each subsequent migration.
Use fixed matched task order/seeds and multiple timing repetitions; retain raw paired observations.
Keep equality/negative results. Do not equate lines of code or injected-fault outcomes with developer productivity.
Pilot S3 and S5 first; complete six-task suite only if pilot is informative.
If both arms are equal, report it and reconsider ontology-centered framing.
No external services, field data, user study, or liveplant claim required or implied.
Steam-water return loops are cyclic: use complete coupled-loop recomputation, not an assumed acyclic dependency schedule.
